# Principles

Named rules that steer how agents design, build and verify. Steer an agent by name ("apply prove it works"); the agent must say which decision each principle changed.
Source files live in [`plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/`](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/). Each has a stable `id` that other skills, profiles and (later) the knowledge base use to refer to it.

## Core

| Principle | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| [Attack the Premise](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/attack-the-premise.md) `attack-the-premise` | Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. | Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it. |
| [Build the Lever](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/build-the-lever.md) `build-the-lever` | Any non-trivial work. | Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns. |
| [Exhaust the Design Space](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/exhaust-the-design-space.md) `exhaust-the-design-space` | A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. | Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing. |
| [Experience First](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/experience-first.md) `experience-first` | Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. | Choose user delight over implementation convenience. |
| [Foundational Thinking](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/foundational-thinking.md) `foundational-thinking` | Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share. | Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious. |
| [Laziness Protocol](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/laziness-protocol.md) `laziness-protocol` | Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. | Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem. |
| [Minimize Reader Load](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/minimize-reader-load.md) `minimize-reader-load` | Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. | Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope. |
| [Outcome-Oriented Execution](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/outcome-oriented-execution.md) `outcome-oriented-execution` | Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. | Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states. |
| [Redesign from First Principles](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/redesign-from-first-principles.md) `redesign-from-first-principles` | Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. | Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one. |
| [Subtract Before You Add](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/subtract-before-you-add.md) `subtract-before-you-add` | Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. | Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base. |

## Architecture

| Principle | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| [Boundary Discipline](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/boundary-discipline.md) `boundary-discipline` | Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. | Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure. |
| [Make Operations Idempotent](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/make-operations-idempotent.md) `make-operations-idempotent` | Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. | Converge to the same end state. |
| [Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis.md) `migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis` | Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. | Migrate and delete in one wave. |
| [Model the Domain](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/model-the-domain.md) `model-the-domain` | Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. | Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals. |
| [Separate Before Serializing Shared State](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/separate-before-serializing-shared-state.md) `separate-before-serializing-shared-state` | Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. | Eliminate the sharing first. |
| [Type System Discipline](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/type-system-discipline.md) `type-system-discipline` | Designing types or a signature in any typed language. | Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries. |

## Verification

| Principle | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| [Explain the Number](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/explain-the-number.md) `explain-the-number` | Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). | Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think. |
| [Fix Root Causes](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/fix-root-causes.md) `fix-root-causes` | Debugging. | Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it. |
| [Prove It Works](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/prove-it-works.md) `prove-it-works` | After a task, before declaring done. | Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles". |
| [Sequence Work into Verifiable Units](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/sequence-verifiable-units.md) `sequence-verifiable-units` | Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. | Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself. |
| [Test Behavior, Not Implementation](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/test-behavior-not-implementation.md) `test-behavior-not-implementation` | Writing, changing, or keeping a test. | Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test. |

## Delegation

| Principle | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| [Guard the Context Window](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/guard-the-context-window.md) `guard-the-context-window` | Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. | Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread. |
| [Never Block on the Human](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/never-block-on-the-human.md) `never-block-on-the-human` | Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. | Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct. |

## Meta

| Principle | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| [Encode Lessons in Structure](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/references/encode-lessons-in-structure.md) `encode-lessons-in-structure` | You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. | Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text. |
